bull_bear.body:
- Deleveraging-first: shed **₹1,364cr** bank-guarantee exposure; reduced outstanding bond exposure; rebuilt cash to **₹880cr**.
- **Dividend restored in 2026** as a signal of restored financial strength.
- Demerger is structured as **no-dilution** for GEPIL holders (they receive JSW Energy shares on top of unchanged GEPIL holding).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Execution / continuity risk** of separating manufacturing: relies on a 5-yr JSW Energy services agreement + building an independent supply chain "very soon" — slippage would pressure core-services delivery.
- **NCLT-sanction / shareholder-vote risk** — the scheme is proposed, not yet sanctioned; retrospective 1-Jul-2025 effective date.
- **No fresh quarterly P&L disclosed** — turnaround metrics are multi-year; investors can't see current-quarter run-rate here.
- Structural dependence on the **thermal-power aftermarket** cycle and on the **GE Vernova / JSW ecosystem** for manufacturing support.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Confident, disciplined-turnaround narrative; candid about Durgapur's underutilization and losses. Emphasis on "value over volume", cash conversion, and no-dilution shareholder alignment. Fully scripted management presentation — **no analyst Q&A to stress-test claims**, so credibility is best judged against the multi-year balance-sheet figures they disclosed.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The **buyer is JSW Energy** — a thermal/RE IPP that already backward-integrates equipment (per companies.csv it holds the GE Power boiler business / Toshiba-JSW TG JV); the 661-acre boiler/pressure-vessel plant plus a 5-yr reserved-capacity agreement deepens JSW's in-house thermal-equipment capability.
- **GEPIL becomes a near-pure asset-light services entity** with a clean balance sheet (cash ₹880cr, net worth ₹483cr) — the demerger is the last big step of the two-year cleanup (after Hydro/Gas slump sale + BHEL settlement).
- The **oOEM (third-party fleet) segment doubling** (₹162cr→₹320cr) is the quiet structural story — servicing non-GE thermal fleets widens the addressable base beyond the captive installed base.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net Worth increased 8x+ from Mar'23 to Mar'26; Bank Balance rose 18x+; Outstanding Bonds reduced from INR 1,956 crores to INR 764 crores.
- Dividend declared in 2026 following significant balance sheet strengthening.
- Hydro & Gas slump sale boosted EBITDA by INR 295 crores; BHEL settlement added ~INR 116 crores to P&L and INR 343 crores cash inflow.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **What Durgapur is:** West Bengal facility making **power boiler components, pressure vessels, pipings, coal mills** for thermal plants; **~661 acres leasehold** (industrial factory unit + residential township).
- **Why exit:** utilization fell to mostly service/non-coal work; **significant underutilization 2023–2025** → **~₹27cr/yr average loss** booked in GEPIL. Management evaluated retention vs demerger and chose demerger to simplify the portfolio.
- **Acquirer:** **JSW Energy Ltd** (listed IPP) — expected to improve facility utilization given the broader Indian power-demand outlook.
- **Structure:** Scheme of Arrangement; going-concern, as-is-where-is; **retrospectively effective 1-Jul-2025** on NCLT sanction.
- **Entitlement:** **139 GEPIL shares → 10 JSW Energy shares** (third-party independent valuers + formal Fairness Opinion). **GEPIL shareholding unchanged / no dilution** — shareholders keep full GEPIL stake AND get direct JSW Energy shares.
- **Continuity safeguard:** **5-year manufacturing services agreement with JSW Energy** reserves capacity at pre-agreed schedules/pricing so core-services execution isn't disrupted; independent supply chain being built in parallel ("full independence very soon").
- **Governance:** Board unanimously approved; shareholders invited to vote.

deepdive.thesis: GE Power India is executing a hard turnaround into an **asset-light thermal-power services** company, and is now carving out its last heavy-manufacturing drag. Two years of "value over volume" took **net worth ₹57cr → ₹483cr** (>8x), **EBITDA −₹251cr (FY23) → +₹277cr (FY26)**, **cash −₹66cr (2023) → ₹880cr (Mar-26)** (18x), shed **₹1,364cr of bank-guarantee exposure**, lifted the ICRA rating to **BBB+ stable**, and restored a dividend. The capstone: **demerging the loss-making Durgapur boiler/pressure-vessel plant to JSW Energy** (139 GEPIL : 10 JSW Energy shares, no GEPIL dilution) to remove a ~₹27cr/yr average loss and sharpen the pure-services focus.

open.item: Normalized (ex one-offs) FY26 EBITDA margin was 11% at the entity level (18% at Q4 quarter level); management stated the 'base is set' and expects future years to be at least at par with this normalized level, while declining to give a specific forward range
Approximately 85-90% of the core services order-in-hand as of 31 March 2026 is expected to be executed within FY27

Targeted core-services fleet market is about INR 3,500-4,000 crore annually; company currently holds roughly 18% share and aims to grow that share, stabilize over the next year, before considering further expansion into other areas
Durgapur business demerged to JSW Energy on NCLT sanction (139 GEPIL : 10 JSW Energy shares, no GEPIL dilution), retrospectively effective 1-Jul-2025
Achieve full independent supply chain post-demerger (bridged by 5-yr JSW Energy manufacturing services agreement)
No disruption to manufacturing/fabrication support for the core services business through the demerger transition
open.promised: no disruption to order execution / service delivery milestone

open.item: Board recommended an exceptional dividend payout of 70% of face value (INR 7 per equity share), the highest in at least 10 years, subject to shareholder approval at the ensuing AGM
Company has been declared L1 (lowest bidder) on one FGD project, seen as restoring confidence in the FGD pillar after earlier policy-related slowness
NTPC granted suppliers a general amnesty of 8.5 months' time extension on Lot 1/2/3 projects; company pursuing further claims/cost relief but declined to size the amount
